vision.title: The Adventure Begins

inputs.title: The Adventure Begins
inputs.logline: When eager young Keen sails away from home and into a storm, he discovers that courage is not looking fearless — it is hearing someone else need him, feeling the gulp, and going anyway.

orderedEvents.text: Tall flowers sway gently in the warm breeze. Some stretch high above the grass, with long soft necks and bright open petals full of pollen. FUZZBY and ZENNY weave between them collecting pollen from flower to flower. Fine golden pollen dusts their paws and trails softly through the air. Zenny works with smooth calm precision — neat, efficient, graceful. Fuzzby does not. He zig-zags wildly through the air, humming loudly to himself as he works.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY, BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY…
He dips low into a flower, scoops up pollen — then overdoes it and spins sideways into a leaf. FWIP. He bounces back into the air and straightens up proudly.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: Nailed it.
Zenny glides up beside him. Watches him for a beat.

beats.storyBeat: The episode opens at bee scale in a bright flower field: Zenny’s graceful competence and Fuzzby’s chaotic overconfidence are instantly legible. Fuzzby’s first pollen dive becomes a crash he rebrands as mastery, planting the whole episode’s comic idea that bravado is not the same as courage.
beats.want: Fuzzby wants to collect pollen like an impressive professional and be seen doing it.
beats.need: He needs to know he belongs even when his body betrays his grand self-image.
beats.kidRead: Funny bee zooms too fast, hits a leaf, bounces back and pretends he meant it.
beats.adultRead: A tiny performer is already covering embarrassment with status — lovable because the mask is transparent.
beats.emotionalIntent: Start with easy laughter, high energy and immediate character contrast, with no danger yet beyond Fuzzby’s own momentum.

beats.need: He needs to stop treating every mistake as something to hide.

beats.need: He needs permission to be unsure and still go.
beats.kidRead: Keen packs and checks and checks again before sailing away.
beats.adultRead: A child is performing independence in front of a parent who can see every crack and chooses not to crush it.
beats.emotionalIntent: Make the goodbye ordinary and tactile before it becomes ceremonial.

vision.premise: Keen leaves his Mum and the safety of home, sails into weather bigger than he expected, saves Squeaky before he has any crystal power, and is welcomed into the Crystal Bears when the courage already inside him finds its visible form.
vision.dramaticQuestion: Can Keen stop performing bravery long enough to discover the real thing — acting through fear for someone who needs him?
vision.theme: Courage is not the absence of fear; it is the scared part and the brave part moving together.
vision.externalJourney: Keen packs a small sailboat, says goodbye at the pier, meets Squeaky, gets lost in a storm, follows Squeaky toward help, dives underwater to free him from a net, reaches Crystal Cove, receives the Aquamarine in his father’s wristbands, and walks into his new family.
vision.internalJourney: Keen begins trying to prove he is ready and fearless, keeps covering wobble with confidence, meets his real valley when the storm strips away map, boat and certainty, then acts without hesitation for Squeaky and learns that the fear he felt did not cancel his courage — it made the courage real.
vision.relationshipChanges: Keen and his Mum move from close protection to trusted distance through the wristbands. Keen and Squeaky become friends through play, danger, rescue and mutual rescue. Aida moves from distant witness to welcomer, completing Mum’s act of letting go with a found-family welcome. Fuzzby shifts from comic self-importance to genuine awe of Keen.
vision.emotionalCurve: Warm morning play and goodbye, then comic buoyancy, then cooling uncertainty, storm panic, the underwater nadir with one charged wordless wristband beat, explosive relief, soft welcome, ceremonial belonging, and a golden-hour laugh that still remembers the boat and the goodbye.
vision.comedyCurve: Fuzzby’s proud-bumbler pollen escalation opens the episode, then Keen inherits the same cover-up grammar in his wobble and map confusion. As danger rises, comedy narrows into release valves — Fuzzby’s emergency crashes, Zenny’s dry precision, the dolphin-cowboy ride — before ending with Fuzzby’s honey-friendship overcommitment.
vision.setupPayoffMap: Fuzzby’s 'Nailed it' cover-up sets the comic grammar for Keen’s 'Still got it.' Mum’s vacant wristbands are handed over with no glow, then self-glow underwater when Keen finds courage from within, then receive Aquamarine gems in the ceremony. Aida’s bowl vision of pier, boat and Mum pays off in her timely rescue beacon and later message home. Squeaky’s playful chatter pays off as urgent signaling in the storm and mutual rescue at the surface.
vision.visualMotifs: Empty gold wristbands becoming faint aqua, then crystal-set azure; small figures against wide water; paws closing around objects of trust; warm home receding into distance; storm-grey swallowing horizon; rose-pink beacon cutting through rain; wet sand and droplets after cost; final golden beach path with the group moving as one.
vision.sonicMotifs: Fuzzby’s manic buzz-crash rhythm; Zenny’s dry stillness after chaos; Aida’s low bowl tone blooming into rose light; Keen’s repeated self-steadying phrase; Squeaky’s chirps shifting from play to distress to relief; Aquamarine’s B-note emerging from muffled underwater hush into the group chord.
vision.climax: Underwater, with Squeaky tangled and the massive wave gathering, Keen sees his father’s vacant wristbands faintly glow, centers himself, pulls with everything he has, tears the net free, is thrown by the wave, and is then carried back up by the friend he saved.
vision.resolution: Aida awards Keen the Aquamarine, the crystal splits into two gems that settle into his father’s wristbands, the group swamps him in a hug, and the phrase from Mum’s goodbye returns as a found-family truth: wherever he goes, he will not be alone.
vision.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, buoyant belonging with a visible trace of cost — the storm has passed and everyone laughs, but Keen’s boat is gone, Mum had to let him go, and the wristbands carry both loss and home.

orderedEvents.text: Tall flowers sway gently in the warm breeze. Some stretch high above the grass, with long soft necks and bright open petals full of pollen. FUZZBY and ZENNY weave between them collecting pollen from flower to flower. Fine golden pollen dusts their paws and trails softly through the air. Zenny works with smooth calm precision — neat, efficient, graceful. Fuzzby does not. He zig-zags wildly through the air, humming loudly to himself as he works.

He dips low into a flower, scoops up pollen — then overdoes it and spins sideways into a leaf. FWIP. He bounces back into the air and straightens up proudly.

orderedEvents.text: Nailed it.
Zenny glides up beside him. Watches him for a beat.

beats.storyBeat: The episode opens at bee scale in a bright flower field: Zenny’s graceful competence and Fuzzby’s chaotic overconfidence are instantly legible. beats.adultRead: A tiny performer is already covering embarrassment with status — lovable because the mask is transparent.

treatments.name: Treatment 1 — The Chase That Cannot Quite Keep Up
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience enters at bee scale inside a sunny pollen corridor and immediately feels the fun of velocity: Fuzzby is not introduced as a portrait, but as a moving problem the frame is trying to forgive. Children read speed, bounce, pollen and crash; adults read a tiny performer trying to turn embarrassment into status. The scene begins as pure play, then the thunder makes the same momentum feel suddenly exposed.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Fuzzby’s want governs the scene: he wants to look like a brilliant professional while his body keeps providing evidence against him. Zenny remains the stabilising witness, not a co-chaos participant. The emotional point is not that Fuzzby fails; it is that he instantly edits failure into triumph because being visibly wrong feels too small to bear.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary comic mechanism: escalating overcommitment. Fuzzby’s first over-fast pollen scoop becomes the FWIP crash, the accidental pollen moustache becomes self-appointed status, the attempt to fix the status mark widens it, and the storm-pressure boast sends him straight into a flower. The thunder turn uses anticipation-to-reversal: a sound big enough to change the scene meets Fuzzby’s tiny attempt to claim it as part of his act.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Fuzzby is always in committed travel: chest leading, wings working too hard, altitude porpoising, every correction overcorrected. His pride is physical before verbal — he straightens after the FWIP as if the leaf were part of the plan. The line “Nailed it.” lands because his body is still recovering. Zenny’s performance is economical: calm pollen work, a precise glide beside him, withheld amusement, then genuine sky-attention at the thunder. Same thunder, different bodies: Fuzzby wobbles and annexes it into performance; Zenny becomes more still and smaller in delivery.
treatments.visualGrammar: Forgiving chase grammar: the camera travels behind and beside the bees through a playable flower corridor, not face-to-face and not locked to safe observation. The opening frame already contains motion: Fuzzby, about 14 inches, and Zenny, about 12 inches, share the same camera depth with open corridor space ahead; Fuzzby’s path is jagged within that corridor while Zenny’s path is a clean thread. Golden loose pollen hangs in the air as visible evidence of movement; no sacks, baskets or loads.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera follows Fuzzby slightly late, with enough softness in the chase that children never lose geography. It does not protect him from leaving the frame edge for a breath, because his character exceeds containment. When Zenny matters, the camera abandons Fuzzby’s noise just long enough for her stillness to become the joke or the warning. No permanent screen sides: geography is held by depth, scale, and relative motion, not assigned lanes.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Movement is Fuzzby’s mask; stillness is Zenny’s judgement and care. In the comedy unit, Fuzzby’s frantic diagonals repeatedly cross the calm line of Zenny’s work. In the storm unit, the contrast flips in meaning: his movement becomes denial, her stillness becomes alertness. The scene’s shape is therefore not “busy then quiet,” but “movement reinterpreted by weather.”
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth is a corridor of tall flowers, soft necks and high petals that make the bees feel tiny and the field feel playful rather than dangerous. Foreground stems occasionally wipe the frame as the camera chases, while background flowers sway gently until the thunder subtly tightens the space. Leaves are not props waiting for impact; they are springy participants that prove weight through bend, recoil and pollen burst.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The first three beats play as one 28–30 second comedy climb if performance supports it: Stage 1, busy pollen collection and first FWIP; Stage 2, moustache status and Zenny’s dry puncture; Stage 3, fixing makes it worse and triggers the chain-reaction tumble. The storm turn compresses to roughly 12–15 seconds: thunder interrupts, Fuzzby rebrands it, Zenny names the weather, Fuzzby boasts under pressure and is instantly contradicted by the flower. No padding between causes; each new action worsens or redefines the last.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by changed point of view or comic punctuation only. The comedy unit can live in no more than three motivated views: chase-with-Fuzzby, Zenny-as-fixed-witness, and the environment participating in the tumble. The storm unit cuts only when the scene’s knowledge changes: sky sound, Zenny’s warning, Fuzzby’s pressure boast contradicted by impact. No automatic action/consequence/reaction pattern; reactions are held only when they are the joke or the warning.
treatments.openingImage: A bee-height moving corridor of tall warm flowers: Fuzzby and Zenny at the same depth, small and readable, with open space ahead. Zenny glides in a clean line; Fuzzby wobbles into the corridor already mid-zig-zag, humming “BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY, BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY…” as loose golden pollen trails behind him.
treatments.closingImage: After the storm warning and his brave little pressure boast, Fuzzby is stuck in a flower again, pollen trembling around him as the warm field has begun to feel less safe. Zenny’s quiet sighing presence nearby tells us this is funny — but the sky has changed the room.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not make this a neat tracking master with two bees politely visible. The frame must have to work for Fuzzby. Let stems briefly occlude him, let his altitude threaten the top and bottom of the composition, and let Zenny’s steadiness be discovered rather than parked. The danger is over-clean readability; the cure is experiential chase with honest geography.

treatments.name: Treatment 2 — Zenny’s Calm Field, Fuzzby’s Weather System
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience experiences the scene as a calm, precise world repeatedly invaded by Fuzzby’s personal storm before the real storm arrives. The comedy comes from contrast: a graceful pollen routine is so orderly that every Fuzzby interruption feels enormous. Children laugh because the loud bee keeps bonking the quiet world; adults enjoy Zenny’s affectionate refusal to overreact.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Zenny’s experience governs the camera: she is trying to complete a simple, peaceful task beside someone who turns pollen collection into a parade. Fuzzby’s need is still present — he wants to be impressive and belong — but we read it through Zenny’s measured tolerance. The emotional warmth is that she does not abandon him; her dry witness is a form of companionship.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary comic mechanism: movement against stillness, with deadpan observation as the punchline. Fuzzby’s chaos is funny because Zenny’s calm line gives it a ruler. The moustache gag runs on concealment-to-revelation, then status change: accidental pollen becomes “official,” then “officially nuts.” The storm turn changes the stillness from comic judgement into real attention.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Zenny’s body is the scene’s metronome: smooth pollen collection, tiny efficient paw motions, a slow arrival beside Fuzzby, an almost-withheld laugh, then a clean still look to the sky. Fuzzby is the disruption: he crosses, overshoots, corrects too late, puffs his chest, and tries to sell each accident as intentional. His “Nailed it.” is performed as rank-saving; his “Good thing I work well under pressure.” is already too inflated to survive contact with reality.
treatments.visualGrammar: Composed contrast grammar: the frame gives Zenny’s calm path enough order that Fuzzby’s invasions redraw it. The opening is still forgiving chase staging, not a portrait: both bees share the same camera depth, Fuzzby 14 inches and Zenny 12 inches, with corridor space ahead, but the camera’s emotional anchor is Zenny’s steady glide. Fuzzby cuts through that order like a loose scribble of honey-gold pollen.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera stays patient with Zenny and lets Fuzzby enter, exit and disturb the composition. It may remain still when Zenny is processing, but only because stillness means judgement or warning. It may let Fuzzby blur across the frame rather than chase every loop. No fixed sides: Fuzzby’s position is allowed to migrate as long as his larger size, faster motion and Zenny’s smaller calm precision keep attribution clear.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Stillness is active. Zenny’s pause after “Nailed it.” is not empty; it is her deciding how much of the obvious truth to say. Fuzzby’s movement continually begs to be admired, but Zenny’s held looks puncture him more cleanly than any extra business could. When thunder comes, Zenny’s stillness sharpens; Fuzzby’s movement becomes nervous denial disguised as showmanship.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: The rainforest field is arranged as a gentle workplace: flower heads at multiple depths, pollen motes drifting in warm light, stems making vertical measures of calm. Fuzzby disturbs these layers, knocking pollen out of neat depth into messy clouds. The real thunder slightly dims and cools the far depth first, so Zenny appears to notice the space changing before Fuzzby admits it.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Beats 1.B1–1.B3 form a compact contrast routine: calm work established, Fuzzby’s first crash rebranded, moustache status teased, fix attempt expands into tumble. The scene should feel like Zenny has been interrupted three times, not like Fuzzby has been given unlimited business. Beats 1.B4–1.B5 are a clipped tonal pivot: thunder, Fuzzby’s performance wobble, Zenny’s plain warning, Fuzzby’s boast, immediate flower contradiction.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts favour changed emotional authority. We cut to Zenny when her reaction is the scene’s meaning, not because coverage requires it. We cut to Fuzzby when he has physically created new evidence against himself. We cut to the environment when the field itself participates in the gag or the weather shift. The withheld laugh and the storm warning earn their own held attention; everything else is brisk.
treatments.openingImage: Zenny moves through a tall-flower corridor with smooth, precise pollen work. In the same depth plane, Fuzzby rockets into view beside her, larger and louder, already mid-hum with open corridor ahead and a crooked pollen trail drawing his instability across her calm path.
treatments.closingImage: Zenny remains small and still beside the flower that has swallowed Fuzzby’s latest confidence. The earlier golden pollen comedy is still visible on him and in the air, but the distant sky has cooled; her sigh lands as affection edged with warning.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Resist the temptation to chase Fuzzby constantly. If we always follow the loudest motion, we lose the double-act. Let the frame be brave enough to hold Zenny while Fuzzby causes mayhem around her; her stillness is not safe staging, it is the scene’s opinion. The challenge is to make calm visually active.

treatments.name: Treatment 3 — The Flower Field Performs the Joke
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience feels as if the rainforest itself is playing along with the bees. Flowers sway, pollen floats, leaves spring back, petals receive Fuzzby too eagerly, and the first thunder makes the whole playground inhale. Children see a living obstacle course; adults read a world gently exposing Fuzzby’s self-image without cruelty.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The emotional point of view belongs to the environment as witness and participant: the field is warm, generous, and physically truthful. Fuzzby can claim mastery, but the leaf bend, pollen smear and petal trap tell the honest version. Zenny understands that honesty immediately; Fuzzby needs three escalating lessons from the world before the weather interrupts.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary comic mechanism: environmental participation. The leaf’s FWIP, the pollen moustache, the smear, the chain-reaction tumble and the final flower-stuck button are all the world answering Fuzzby’s bravado. Secondary mechanism: hiding failure. Fuzzby repeatedly tries to rename what the environment has plainly revealed.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Fuzzby treats every flower like a stage entrance and every accident like applause. His body leads too hard into each object; the world pushes back with clear force. He straightens after impact, puffs the chest, and tries to make status out of pollen. Zenny reads the evidence, not the speech: she glides in, studies the pollen result, offers the dry tease, then shifts from amused observer to weather-reader at thunder.
treatments.visualGrammar: Participatory space grammar: the camera discovers actions through foreground leaves, pollen clouds and petal openings rather than cleanly waiting for impacts. The opening still honours the required forgiving chase staging: Fuzzby 14 inches and Zenny 12 inches at the same camera depth, with open corridor ahead. But the corridor is alive — swaying stems make a moving maze, and the camera’s path is occasionally negotiated with the plants.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera is bee-height and embedded in the flower field, sometimes following Fuzzby, sometimes letting the next environmental consequence arrive first. It can lead to a leaf for comic inevitability or arrive late to a pollen aftermath when that is funnier than impact. Zenny is found as the one creature not being bossed around by the field. No assigned screen sides; continuity comes from the mapped corridor, recurring flower landmarks and the contrast between Fuzzby’s jagged travel and Zenny’s clean glide.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Movement belongs not only to Fuzzby but to the environment: flowers sway, leaves recoil, pollen blooms outward, petals settle after swallowing him. Zenny’s stillness is the only non-reactive element until thunder, when the whole field stills for a breath. That environmental pause is the tonal turn: the playground has heard something bigger.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth carries the story. Early depth is open and welcoming, with pollen suspended in warm light and flowers stretching above the bees like friendly towers. Fuzzby’s crashes convert tidy depth into messy clouds and bouncing foreground reactions. At thunder, distant depth darkens and the flower corridor seems taller; the same environment that made him funny now makes him small.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The comedy unit is three environmental answers: first the leaf answers Fuzzby’s overdone scoop with FWIP; then pollen answers his pride by becoming a moustache and smear; then the field answers his recovery attempts with a chain reaction. The storm unit is a single environmental reclassification: thunder changes the field from playground to warning system, and Fuzzby’s pressure boast is immediately disproved by another flower.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated by the environment changing the truth. We cut when a leaf has become a spring, when pollen has become a moustache, when a smear has become worse, when thunder has changed the field’s behaviour, or when the final flower trap gives the button. We do not cut simply to check every face. Zenny’s reaction is earned only after the world has made the evidence undeniable.
treatments.openingImage: At bee height, tall flowers sway like soft towers and a corridor opens ahead. Fuzzby and Zenny share depth, readable in their 14-inch and 12-inch scale difference; Fuzzby’s jagged hum kicks loose a drifting ribbon of golden pollen while Zenny’s clean glide barely disturbs it.
treatments.closingImage: A flower settles around Fuzzby after his pressure boast, its petals gently quivering with the impact. Loose pollen floats in the cooler air, Zenny nearby with the tired knowledge that the field has answered him again, and the storm gathers beyond the once-playful blooms.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not reduce the field to background decoration behind character business. The plants must have timing, weight and opinion. Let the lens be low enough that a leaf recoil feels large, and let pollen clouds briefly obscure information so the audience discovers the gag through the world’s reaction. The risk is generic garden prettiness; the cure is environment as comic co-performer.

treatmentSelection.selectedTreatment: Treatment 1 — The Chase That Cannot Quite Keep Up, strengthened with Treatment 3’s field-as-comic-co-performer
combinedFrom: Treatment 1 — The Chase That Cannot Quite Keep Up
Treatment 3 — The Flower Field Performs the Joke
treatmentSelection.governingAudienceExperience: The audience is pulled into a bee-height pollen chase that can barely contain Fuzzby’s self-mythologising speed, then feels the same playful corridor inhale when thunder turns his performance into exposed nerves.
treatmentSelection.rationale: Treatment 1 is the governing spine because it understands the scene’s truth: Fuzzby’s bravado is not random comedy, it is a tiny status performance happening while his body keeps betraying him, with Zenny as the stabilising witness who makes the joke warm. It also best answers the user ambition: opening in motion, forgiving chase staging, same-depth Fuzzby/Zenny scale, playable corridor ahead, no sacks or loads, compact 1.B1–1.B3 comedy climb, and a shorter 1.B4–1.B5 storm turn. Its camera is not safe coverage; it has a relationship to Fuzzby’s overcommitment and Zenny’s stillness, and it allows the frame to work without losing child readability. Treatment 3 should be folded in for visual memorability: the rainforest must not sit behind the gag, but physically answer Fuzzby through leaf recoil, pollen bloom, petal swallow, and the field’s brief stilling at thunder. That gives the comedy texture and makes the tonal turn visible in the world. The combined approach keeps relationship and emotional point of view primary while letting the environment become honest evidence against Fuzzby’s claims.
treatmentSelection.rejectionChecks: Rejected Treatment 2 as the governing treatment: its Zenny-anchored calm-field approach has warmth and deadpan value, but as the main grammar it risks patient composed observation becoming safe camera placement, with Fuzzby repeatedly invading a stable frame. That can drift toward fixed visual order, habitual interruption/reaction punctuation, and a scene opinion delivered through coverage-like holds rather than through the chase experience. Rejected Treatment 3 as the sole treatment: its environmental participation is excellent as a layer, but if the environment owns the emotional point of view, the scene can become a living obstacle course and lose the heart between Fuzzby’s need to be admired and Zenny’s affectionate refusal to over-admire him. Treatment 1 passes the anti-pattern checks because it does not depend on fixed character lanes, keeping all characters visible, automatic action/consequence/reaction coverage, safe camera placement, repeated close-up punctuation, mechanical shot counts, generic cinematic language, or merely illustrating the script. The selected pass must preserve that discipline: no permanent screen sides, no neat tracking master, no face-to-face portrait opening, no padding, and no extra business that is not caused by Fuzzby’s overcommitment, Zenny’s witnessing, the pollen/flower physics, or the storm turn.

scene.purpose: Open the episode in pure bee-scale play, making Fuzzby’s proud overcommitment and Zenny’s calm witnessing instantly legible before thunder reinterprets the same motion as exposed nerves.
scene.dramaticQuestion: Can Fuzzby keep turning visible failure into status when the world stops feeling like a game?
scene.connectionFromPreviousScene: Episode opening; the audience arrives already inside motion, pollen, and the flower corridor rather than meeting the characters in portrait.
scene.handoverToNextScene: The field remains funny but no longer fully safe: Fuzzby is stuck again, Zenny has named the storm, and the weather pressure is now active.

beats.sourceScript: The episode opens at bee scale in a bright flower field: Zenny’s graceful competence and Fuzzby’s chaotic overconfidence are instantly legible. Fuzzby’s first pollen dive becomes a crash he rebrands as mastery, planting the whole episode’s comic idea that bravado is not the same as courage.

orderedEvents.text: Tall flowers sway gently in the warm breeze. Some stretch high above the grass, with long soft necks and bright open petals full of pollen. FUZZBY and ZENNY weave between them collecting pollen from flower to flower. Fine golden pollen dusts their paws and trails softly through the air. Zenny works with smooth calm precision — neat, efficient, graceful. Fuzzby does not. He zig-zags wildly through the air, humming loudly to himself as he works.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY, BIZZY-BIZZY-BIZZY…
He dips low into a flower, scoops up pollen — then overdoes it and spins sideways into a leaf. FWIP. He bounces back into the air and straightens up proudly.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: Nailed it.
Zenny glides up beside him. Watches him for a beat.

beats.whatChanges: The flower field changes from a pretty setting into an active comic corridor, and Fuzzby changes from busy worker to exposed performer: his first big move visibly fails, then he claims it as success.
beats.whoDrives: Fuzzby drives the change through over-fast, over-proud pollen collecting; the leaf and pollen prove the truth of his weight and momentum.
beats.audienceAnticipation: Children anticipate the fast bee will crash into something; adults anticipate the instant status-edit after the crash. Zenny’s smooth line lets the audience measure how unnecessary Fuzzby’s chaos is.
beats.actionOrChoice: Fuzzby barrels through the pollen corridor humming, dips too hard into a flower, scoops pollen, overcorrects sideways into a springy leaf, bounces back, and chooses a proud recovery instead of absorbing the mistake.
beats.consequence: The FWIP gives the field a voice: leaf bend, recoil, pollen burst, and Fuzzby’s still-recovering body all contradict the line that follows.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: The handover is Fuzzby upright in a proud little pose that has not finished wobbling, with Zenny’s calm competence still nearby; the scene can now escalate the gap between his claimed mastery and visible evidence.

emotionContract.entryState: Charged with self-important speed, already mid-zig-zag and wanting his work to read as brilliant.
emotionContract.pressure: He is sharing the corridor with Zenny’s visible competence, so every messy correction exposes him by comparison.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: He chooses to reframe the leaf collision as planned success rather than let the crash sit as a crash.
emotionContract.exitState: Proud but physically betrayed: upright, chest-forward, still recovering from impact.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: His path jaggedly porpoises through pollen while Zenny’s path stays clean; after the FWIP his body has not fully settled before he declares victory.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The audience now knows Fuzzby’s pride will keep outrunning his control.

comedyContract.setup: A tiny pollen-working corridor where Zenny’s neat efficiency and Fuzzby’s chaotic speed are both readable at the same depth.
comedyContract.expectation: Fuzzby’s loud rhythm promises busy competence and clean pollen collection.
comedyContract.disruption: He overdoes the scoop, spins sideways into the leaf, and the leaf FWIPs him back into the air.
comedyContract.button: Fuzzby’s recovery line lands while his body is still proving the opposite.
comedyContract.hold: Hold just long enough on the proud recovery for the audience to read leaf recoil, drifting pollen, and Zenny’s unruffled contrast before the next status gag begins.

physicalStaging.staysVisible: Fuzzby, the flower mouth he dives into, the springy leaf, the pollen trail, and Zenny’s steady working line remain readable through the continuous chase geography.
physicalStaging.contactAndWeight: Fuzzby’s sideways momentum visibly depresses the leaf; the leaf bends under him, stores the force, then snaps him back with pollen bursting from the contact.
physicalStaging.payoffShape: A jagged dive becomes a sideways smear, then a clean elastic FWIP back to an over-proud upright hover that cannot hide its wobble.
prohibitedStaging: Do not make the leaf a flat trampoline with no bend or weight.
Do not cut away before the body-to-leaf cause is readable.
Do not park both bees in a neat tracking master that removes Fuzzby’s containment problem.

beats.sourceScript: Fuzzby escalates from pollen collector to self-appointed official by accidentally wearing a pollen moustache. Zenny’s almost-withheld laugh and dry tease make the relationship the punchline: she sees exactly who he is and stays beside him anyway.

orderedEvents.text: He zooms to another flower, humming louder, and sticks his whole face into it. A beat. He pulls back out completely dusted in pollen like a fuzzy yellow moustache. Zenny tries not to laugh.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: Do I look official?

orderedEvents.speaker: Zenny
orderedEvents.text: Yes Fuzzby Officially nuts!

beats.whatChanges: The accident gains a title: pollen on Fuzzby’s face becomes, in his mind, a mark of rank, while Zenny turns the rank into affectionate puncture.
beats.whoDrives: Fuzzby drives the status inflation; Zenny drives the comic correction.
beats.audienceAnticipation: The audience anticipates Fuzzby will ask to be admired for the accident and that Zenny will not give him the admiration in the form he wants.
beats.actionOrChoice: Fuzzby presents the accidental pollen moustache as if it might make him official; Zenny lets the tiniest amusement nearly surface, then answers with a dry re-title.
beats.consequence: The relationship snaps into focus: he needs the accident upgraded, she names it honestly without leaving him alone in it.
beats.emotionalOrComicHandover: Zenny’s line leaves Fuzzby with a new problem: the status mark he wanted is now a joke on him, so his next instinct is to fix it.

emotionContract.entryState: Puffed up from the first rebrand, looking for confirmation that the pollen accident can become status.
emotionContract.pressure: Zenny’s calm attention is the witness he wants to impress and the witness least likely to be fooled.
emotionContract.choiceOrRealisation: He chooses to invite admiration instead of noticing that the moustache is evidence of the crash.
emotionContract.exitState: Momentarily re-labelled: still proud, but now aware enough of Zenny’s tease to react into the next fix.
emotionContract.observableEvidence: He presents himself chest-forward and asks for the verdict; Zenny’s restraint and dry answer puncture the pose without escalating her body.
emotionContract.heldAfterBeat: The pollen moustache remains visible as both Fuzzby’s invented badge and Zenny’s proof.

comedyContract.setup: Fuzzby accidentally wears a pollen moustache after a crash he has already claimed as success.
comedyContract.expectation: He expects Zenny to validate the moustache as impressive or official.
comedyContract.disruption: Zenny agrees only far enough to turn “official” into the insult-tag of the joke.
comedyContract.hold: Hold on Zenny’s economy and Fuzzby’s proud pose absorbing the re-title before he tries to correct the evidence.

beats.sourceScript: Fuzzby tries to fix the moustache and only makes it worse, then turns the whole field into a chain-reaction tumble. The gag escalates through overcommitment: every attempt to recover becomes a bigger physical confession of failure.

orderedEvents.text: Fuzzby gasps. He wipes at his face. Somehow smears the pollen worse. He dives again toward another flower — clips a branch — tumbles end over end through the air. THUP. THUP. THUP. He lands upside down inside a blossom. Beat. His little legs kick. Then he pops back up.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby

showrunnerJudgement: Pass. I tried to break this on the usual Crystal Bears failure points — safe coverage, neat lanes, automatic reactions, decorative stillness, padded cuts, and generic meadow chaos — but the storyboard keeps the selected experience intact. Fuzzby is introduced as motion and self-mythology, not as a posed character; Zenny functions as the stabilising witness rather than a second source of busyness; the comedy escalates from overcommitment rather than random incident; and the thunder genuinely reinterprets the same movement grammar instead of simply interrupting it. The scene retains the kid door of velocity, pollen and impacts, and the adult door of a tiny performer rebranding embarrassment as status.
treatmentComparison: This is a faithful delivery of Treatment 1 — The Chase That Cannot Quite Keep Up. The first unit preserves the intended 28–30 second comedy climb: chase-with-Fuzzby, moustache status witnessed by Zenny, and worsening recovery into tumble. The camera relationship remains experiential and forgiving rather than locked-off: stems can wipe, Fuzzby can threaten the frame edge, and Zenny’s calm line is discovered through contrast, not parked in a permanent screen lane. The second unit correctly compresses the storm turn: thunder changes the audience’s understanding of the corridor, Fuzzby tries to annex fear into performance, Zenny becomes still and sky-aware, and the final flower impact lands as both laugh and warning. The closing image also matches the treatment’s bittersweet tonal shift: funny stuck Fuzzby, but with the sky having changed the room.
packingJudgement: Packing passes. The split is justified: S1.SH1 is a near-full 29-second comedy climb with three motivated internal views, and adding the 14-second storm/pressure arc would exceed the 30-second Seedance window. The boundary protects a real dramatic and rhythmic change — play-space becoming warning-space — not an avoidable join. There is no empty padding, and the units use the 30-second capacity responsibly.
